title: Output-Length Bound from the Initial State
statement: Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, and fix an input bit string $x$. For every starting label $\ell_0\in\Lambda$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the output produced after $t$ steps from the initial state at $\ell_0$ has length at most $t(t+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: $R\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\Lambda$ is a set of labels.
$P$ is a counter program over $R$ registers and labels in $\Lambda$.
An input bit string $x$ is fixed.
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, $\ell_0$ a label and
$t \in \mathbb{N}$.  Starting from the initial state at $\ell_0$ (all registers
$0$, nothing read, empty output), the output after $t$ steps of $P$ on $x$ has
length at most $t(t+1)$.
